O Hangul organiza letras em blocos siláb: Hangul organizes letters into syllabic blocks. A syllable that begins with a vowel uses ㅇ in the initial position: there it has no sound. Thus, ㅏ becomes 아 and ㅗ becomes 오.

Hangul organizes letters into syllabic blocks. A syllable that begins with a vowel uses ㅇ in the initial position: there it has no sound. Thus, ㅏ becomes 아 and ㅗ becomes 오. The ten basic vowels are ㅏ, ㅑ, ㅓ, ㅕ, ㅗ, ㅛ, ㅜ, ㅠ, ㅡ, and ㅣ. ㅏ approaches “a”; ㅗ is a rounded “o”; ㅜ approaches “u”. ㅓ and ㅡ do not have exact equivalents in English. Shapes with an additional short stroke, such as ㅑ and ㅛ, add an initial “y” sound. In vertical vowels, such as ㅏ and ㅣ, the initial consonant is on the left. On the horizontals, like ㅗ and ㅜ, it is above. Read the blocks as units, without saying the name of each letter.
